questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An isolated physical system transitions from initial state parameter $p_i = 8$ to final configuration $p_f = 16$ while conserving the quantity $\mathcal{E} = p_i^2 + 2p_f$. What is the value of $\mathcal{E}$ in SI units?
questions.explanation: Apply the conservation & invariant balance principles in Rotational Motion (Moment of Inertia & Parallel Axis).

questions.explanation: Apply the conservation & invariant balance principles in Rotational Motion (Rolling Without Slipping).

questions.explanation: Apply the instantaneous rate & gradient law principles in Rotational Motion (Angular Momentum Conservation).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When the amplitude of the driving excitation in a linear resistive medium (resistance $13$ units) is multiplied by $6$, by what factor does the rate of quadratic energy dissipation change?

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical quantity $f(z)$ increases linearly from $0$ to $28$ units over the interval $z \in [0, 7]$. Evaluate $\int_0^{7} f(z)\,dz$.
questions.solution: Area of the right triangle under the linear curve is $\frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 28 = 98$.
questions.explanation: Apply the graphical slope & area integration principles in Rotational Motion (Angular Momentum Conservation).

questions.question: A linear calibration line has slope $15$ and vertical-axis intercept $-8$. At what value of the horizontal coordinate does the output cross zero?
questions.explanation: Apply the graphical slope & area integration principles in Rotational Motion (Rigid Body Toppling).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An interaction reduces the mechanical energy of a body to $\frac{1}{7}$ of its initial value $E_0 = 147\text{ J}$. How much mechanical energy is lost during the interaction?
questions.solution: Dissipated energy $\Delta E = E_0 - E_0/7 = 147 - 21 = 126\text{ J}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the energy efficiency & dissipation principles in Rotational Motion (Rolling Without Slipping).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a mechanical assembly to remain stable, the stiffness parameter $k$ must exceed the critical value $k_c = 22\text{ N/m}$. If the operating stiffness is set to $k = 52\text{ N/m}$, what is the excess stiffness margin $k - k_c$?
questions.solution: The stability margin is $k - k_c = (52) - 22 = 30\text{ N/m}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the critical threshold & equilibrium principles in Rotational Motion (Angular Momentum Conservation).

questions.explanation: Apply the critical threshold & equilibrium principles in Rotational Motion (Rigid Body Toppling).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The frequency response function $H(\omega) = \frac{72}{\omega + 3^2 / \omega}$ for $\omega > 0$ reaches its maximum value at $\omega = \omega_0$. Determine $\omega_0$ and $H(\omega_0)$.
questions.solution: By AM-GM, $\omega + 3^2/\omega \ge 2(3)$ with equality at $\omega_0 = 3$, giving $H_{\max} = \frac{72}{2\cdot 3} = \frac{24}{2}$.
questions.explanation: Apply the resonance & extremum condition principles in Rotational Motion (Moment of Inertia & Parallel Axis).
